cards.text: Three years pass with no war between Aram and Israel, and then Jehoshaphat king of Judah goes down to visit Ahab, the king of Israel. Three quiet years, friend. In my experience, that's EXACTLY when somebody gets an idea.
Ahab turns to his servants. Ramoth-gilead is OURS, he says, and we still haven't taken it from the king of Aram.

cards.question: Ahab wants Ramoth-gilead. So what does he ask his guest Jehoshaphat?

answers.text: To go fight for it with him
To pay Aram a price for it
To ask Aram's king to give it up

cards.question: Jehoshaphat turns Ahab down and keeps Judah out of the fight.

answers.text: True
False

cards.question: Jehoshaphat is in, horses and all. But before anybody marches, what does he ask Ahab to do first?

answers.text: Find out what the LORD says
Find out how big Aram's army is
Find out if Aram will make peace

cards.text: So Ahab assembles about four hundred prophets and asks if he should go to war against Ramoth-gilead or refrain. FOUR HUNDRED prophets, friend, and I can't get four people to answer a group chat.

cards.question: What do Ahab's four hundred prophets tell him?

answers.text: Go up and the Lord will give him the city
Stay home and leave the city to Aram
Wait until Judah's army grows bigger

cards.question: After all four hundred prophets say go, Jehoshaphat still asks if there's a prophet of the LORD they can inquire of.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Ahab admits there's still one man they can inquire of the LORD through. ONE prophet, and Ahab says he hates him.

cards.question: Why does Ahab hate this one prophet of the LORD?

answers.text: He never prophesies anything good for Ahab
He once took sides with the king of Aram
He refused to stand before Ahab's throne

cards.text: The man is Micaiah son of Imlah, and Jehoshaphat replies, "The king should not say that!" Friend, Ahab just said he hates a prophet for bringing bad news, and he said it OUT LOUD, in front of company.

cards.question: After Jehoshaphat speaks up, what does Ahab do about Micaiah?

answers.text: Sends an official to bring him at once
Sends word that he must stay away
Sends the four hundred to argue with him

cards.text: Dressed in royal attire, Ahab and Jehoshaphat sit on their thrones at the threshing floor by the gate of Samaria, with all the prophets prophesying before them. Two kings, two thrones, four hundred prophets, and friend, this is a SHOW.
Then one of the prophets, Zedekiah son of Chenaanah, steps up with iron horns he made for himself. Arts and crafts, at a war meeting.

cards.question: Zedekiah holds up his iron horns. What does he say they mean?

answers.text: Israel will finish off the Arameans
Aram will strike Israel first
The kings should sound the call to war

cards.question: All the prophets say the same thing. They tell Ahab to go up to Ramoth-gilead and ___.

answers.text: triumph
retreat
negotiate

cards.text: Now the messenger who went to get Micaiah coaches him: the prophets are all speaking favorably to the king, so please let your words be like theirs. That's a coworker leaning over before the meeting going, everybody already said yes, just NOD.

cards.question: The messenger wants Micaiah to go along with the crowd. What does Micaiah say?

answers.text: He'll speak whatever the LORD tells him
He promises to agree with the prophets
He'll say nothing at all to the king

cards.text: Micaiah arrives, and Ahab asks him the same question: should we go to war against Ramoth-gilead, or should we refrain? Two kings and four hundred prophets, all waiting on one man.

cards.question: What is Micaiah's first answer to Ahab?

answers.text: Go up and triumph
Wait until next year
Make peace with Aram

cards.question: Ahab finally hears good news from Micaiah and takes it at his word.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Ahab snaps back, "How many times must I make you swear not to tell me anything but the truth in the name of the LORD?" The man finally gets good news and doesn't trust it, like an oven timer that dings WAY too early.
So Micaiah tells what he saw: all Israel scattered on the hills like sheep without a shepherd. And the LORD says these people have no master.

cards.question: In Micaiah's vision, the LORD says scattered Israel has no master. What else does He say about them?

answers.text: Let each one return home in peace
Let them gather for battle again
Let them choose a new king to follow

cards.question: Ahab turns to Jehoshaphat and says this proves what he said about Micaiah.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: While Ahab is busy with his I-told-you-so, Micaiah keeps going. He saw the LORD sitting on His throne, with all the host of heaven standing by Him on His right and on His left.

cards.question: In Micaiah's vision of the throne, what does the LORD ask?

answers.text: Who will entice Ahab to fall at Ramoth-gilead
Who will warn Ahab to stay out of the war
Who will fight for Israel at Ramoth-gilead

cards.text: One suggests this, and another that. Then a spirit comes forward, stands before the LORD and says, "I will entice him."

cards.question: The LORD asks the spirit by what means. The spirit says he'll be a ___ spirit in the mouths of all Ahab's ___.

answers.text: lying
prophets
faithful
soldiers
servants

cards.question: The LORD tells the spirit he will prevail and sends him to do it.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: So Micaiah tells Ahab straight: the LORD has put a lying spirit in the mouths of all these prophets of his, and the LORD has pronounced disaster against him. Four hundred to one, friend, and the one is the guy getting the word from the LORD.
Then Zedekiah, the iron horns guy, walks up and strikes Micaiah in the face. He demands, "Which way did the Spirit of the LORD go when He departed from me to speak with you?"

cards.question: Zedekiah wants to know which way the Spirit went. How does Micaiah answer him?

answers.text: He'll see on the day he hides in an inner room
He'll see on the day Ramoth-gilead falls to Israel
He'll see on the day the king sends him away

cards.question: Now Ahab gives an order about Micaiah. What is it?

answers.text: Put him in prison until Ahab returns
Send him home to his father Imlah
Bring him along to Ramoth-gilead

cards.text: Ahab orders Micaiah taken back to Amon the governor of the city and Joash the king's son, on only bread and water, and in Ahab's words it lasts "until I return safely." Friend, that's a man booking the victory party before the battle even starts.

cards.question: Micaiah tells Ahab that if he ever returns safely, the LORD has not spoken through Micaiah.

answers.text: True
False

cards.text: Then Micaiah adds, "Take heed, all you people!" And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because Ramoth-gilead is still out there and this story is NOT done.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates stop 1. Of its 10 choice cards, 7 are multiple choice (cards 3, 5, 7, 10, 12, 15, 18), 2 are true or false and 1 is fill in the blank. Some of those multiple choice cards should become true or false or fill in the blank.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: "What else does He say about them?" asks the baker to guess the second half of the LORD's line in 1 Kings 22:17. Card 5 gives the first half. The wrong answer "Let them choose a new king to follow" fits "these people have no master" just as well as the right one, so a correct pick comes down to luck. The card should ask about the meaning of the vision instead, for example what the scattered sheep with no master mean for Israel.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The story-isn't-over line reuses the doc's example wording, "And that's where we'll leave it for now," instead of a line written fresh for this passage.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.
